A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DENSE research work. All 15 pages of each were checked, including text, equations, tables, figures, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains appendices, and no material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot node-classification experiments on ten datasets, comparisons with 15 baselines, backbone comparisons, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 4, including Tables 1-3 and Figure 3. These remain original empirical results despite being unchanged.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2-3.5 retain identical bundle sampling, LLM querying, entropy-based and ranking-based supervision, and dynamic bundle refinement. The title change does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same ten datasets spanning citation, Wikipedia, e-commerce, and university webpage graphs. The zero-shot node-classification task and homophilic and heterophilic graph coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all 15 baselines, including SBERT, GPT-4o, GraphMAE, GOFA, and LLM-BP. No comparison method is added, removed, or revised in the reported experiments.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain identical: GPT-4o as the default LLM, bundle size 5, and 100 bundles. Accuracy evaluation, alternative LLM configurations, and experimental controls are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the six ablation variants in Table 3, bundle-size and bundle-count analyses and query comparisons in Figure 3, and the prompt-response case study in Figure 4. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report point accuracies without specified repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Their uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-3 and plotted results in Figure 3 match, as do the qualitative findings. For example, Table 1 reports DENSE accuracies of 75.09 on Cora and 92.51 on Texas in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)-(9), and Theorems 3.1-3.3 retain the same statements, assumptions, and accompanying reasoning. No proof or theoretical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion are unchanged. The revised title explicitly mentions large language models but does not change the claims about bundle supervision, outlier tolerance, convergence, or empirical effectiveness.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the ablations, bundle-size effects, and query reliability are unchanged. Both retain the same applicability limitations concerning attributes that LLMs cannot readily understand and graph structures poorly handled by GNNs.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including the default LLM, bundle parameters, NVIDIA RTX 3090 hardware, and Figure 4 prompt template. No reproducibility details or resource-access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 86 references are unchanged. The positioning relative to graph foundation models and methods using LLM-generated supervision remains the same.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Dynamic Text Bundling Supervision for Zero-Shot Inference on Text-Attributed Graphs' to 'Dynamic Bundling with Large Language Models for Zero-Shot Inference on Text-Attributed Graphs.' The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-4 and Tables 1-3 retain their content, captions, formatting, and placement. The revised title remains a two-line heading within the same first-page layout; there is no figure, table, or layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 explicitly identifies large language models in the title but otherwise retains the same scientific content, evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information. This editorial revision does not establish a meaningful overall improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
